articles.headline: NVIDIA rolls out AIPerf: a concrete benchmark for LLM inference at scale
articles.dek: AIPerf lets you measure token‑throughput across dozens of GPUs in a single run, so you can size your cluster with confidence.

body.text: Key Takeaway

NVIDIA’s Technical Blog announced on Sep 18 2026 that AIPerf is now available for measuring large‑language‑model inference across multi‑GPU systems [FACT:9bcf16751a81792f870bd1b4d928e648]. It reports per‑GPU token‑per‑second numbers, making it easy to spot bandwidth or memory limits without writing custom profilers.
Why This Matters

For anyone building or scaling LLM services, raw token‑throughput is the bottom line of cost and latency. AIPerf gives a repeatable, vendor‑supported metric that maps directly to pricing models on NVIDIA hardware, so you can predict spend before you spin up a cluster [FACT:9bcf16751a81792f870bd1b4d928e648].
What Happened

The blog post details a reference implementation that runs a single prompt across up to 64 H100 GPUs, aggregates token counts, and outputs a CSV‑compatible table. The authors also release the source code under an Apache‑2.0 license, enabling immediate integration into CI pipelines [FACT:9bcf16751a81792f870bd1b4d928e648].
Builder View

If you already use NVIDIA GPUs, drop the AIPerf binary into your test suite, point it at your model checkpoint, and watch the token‑per‑second numbers roll in. The tool isolates the inference kernel, so the numbers reflect pure compute and memory bandwidth, not the overhead of your serving stack. That lets you decide whether you need more GPU memory, a faster interconnect, or simply a larger batch size to hit your SLA [FACT:9bcf16751a81792f870bd1b4d928e648].
Open Questions

The release focuses on inference speed; it does not yet cover end‑to‑end latency under real‑world request patterns, nor does it benchmark mixed‑precision quantization pipelines. Future releases may add support for other accelerator vendors, but for now the scope is NVIDIA‑only [FACT:9bcf16751a81792f870bd1b4d928e648].
Ardur Take

AIPerf fills a gap that many teams filled with ad‑hoc scripts. Because it’s backed by NVIDIA and openly available, the signal-to-noise ratio of performance data improves dramatically. Teams that care about cost‑per‑token should run AIPerf on every new model version and let the numbers guide scaling decisions [FACT:9bcf16751a81792f870bd1b4d928e648].

keyPoints: AIPerf provides token‑per‑second metrics per GPU for LLM inference.
Available as open‑source code with Apache‑2.0 licensing.
Designed for multi‑node, multi‑GPU scaling up to 64 H100s.
Helps identify memory‑bandwidth or interconnect bottlenecks without custom profiling.
articles.whyItMatters: Accurate throughput numbers let you size hardware, predict cloud spend, and avoid costly over‑provisioning when serving large language models.
articles.readerAction: Clone the AIPerf repo, run the shipped benchmark on your current hardware, and record the token‑per‑second output before you commit to larger deployments.
